papers.title: Vertical distribution of prey and vegetation structure shape bat and ground-dwelling mammal activity in a temperate forest
papers.abstract: Vertical structural complexity shapes resource availability throughout forest ecosystems. However, how mobile consumers respond to this variation across the vertical profile remains poorly understood, particularly for taxonomic groups differing in their ability to access different vertical layers. In this study, we examine how the activity of flying and ground-dwelling small mammals respond to resource distribution and stand structure across the vertical forest profile. We combined paired acoustic bat surveys conducted in the canopy and understorey with ground-based camera trap surveys of small, ground-dwelling mammals, alongside layer-specific measurements of invertebrate prey abundance and LiDAR-derived vegetation structure. Bat activity varied across the vertical profile in line with known foraging ecomorphology; open and edge-foraging specialists were more frequently detected in the canopy, while forest-interior foraging species were more frequently detected in the understorey. Across mammal taxonomic groups, dietary specialists tracked invertebrate abundance independently of vertical layer, whereas dietary generalists showed no relationship to prey abundance. This suggests that trophic specialisation, rather than locomotion mode, determines the strength of bottom-up coupling between invertebrates and their mammalian predators. In contrast, the structural drivers of activity differed strongly between the two taxonomic groups and vertical layers, indicating that structural niche partitioning does not follow the same rules as trophic coupling. Bat activity showed a clutter-versus-resource trade-off and ground-level structural conditions shaped ground-dwelling mammal activity more strongly than canopy-associated attributes. These results show that structural niche partitioning in forest consumer communities is determined by taxon-specific structural characteristics rather than by a single common gradient of habitat quality. Vertically explicit sampling designs are therefore essential to avoid incomplete inference about the environmental drivers of activity, especially for canopy-associated species.

papers.title: TreeCLIP: a source-controlled evaluation of frozen 2D foundation-model features for tree-species clustering from LiDAR
papers.abstract: Complete code, configuration, result files, and the pre-registration of the frozen 3D baseline for the manuscript Frozen 2D Foundation-Model Features Cluster Tree Species in LiDAR Point Clouds More Coherently Than the Evaluated Geometric Descriptors: A Source-Controlled Evaluation (under revision at PFG – Journal of Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Geoinformation Science; preprint DOI: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-10238136/v1). The pipeline renders each individual-tree LiDAR point cloud into six PCA-aligned height-coded depth views, encodes them with frozen 2D vision foundation models (CLIP, DINOv2, supervised-ImageNet, and random-init controls), and evaluates unsupervised species clustering under matched dimensions with acquisition-source confounding treated as a first-class control (within-source residuals, per-block and leave-one-source-out analyses, and a pre-registered frozen 3D OpenShape/PointBERT baseline). Every number in the manuscript traces to a JSON result file under runs/protocol_v2/gen/ in this archive. The point-cloud datasets themselves are not redistributed; the README lists their DOIs and licenses. MIT license.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Do green roofs support urban bird diversity? Evidence from citizen science observations in Shanghai
papers.abstract: Green roofs hold substantial potential for supporting urban biodiversity conservation. Researchers have investigated how multidimensional characteristics of green roofs (e.g., 2D spatial and 3D structural features) influence habitat suitability for urban avifauna. Nevertheless, reliance on labor-intensive field surveys for bird observations has confined research to finite scales. Additionally, oversimplified proxies for vegetation structure (e.g., coverage and average height) overlook the structural complexity jointly formed by vegetation with divergent morphologies. To address these limitations, this study integrates citizen-science bird data with remote-sensing-derived roof metrics in Shanghai, applying Negative Binomial (NB) and Zero-inflated NB models to investigate the associations between multidimensional roof features and bird abundance and species richness at large scales across multiple buffers, while accounting for adjacent greenspace features and observation effort. Results show modest improvements in model performance when roof- and greenspace-level variables were considered jointly, suggesting that roof attributes may provide limited but complementary explanatory information beyond surrounding greenspace conditions. Roof-level associations and cross-level interactions with both avian metrics were more evident within 125 and 250 m buffers, but their direction and magnitude varied across spatial scales and surrounding landscape context, indicating scale dependence and context sensitivity. Several roof factors, including NDVI, relative land surface temperature, woody vegetation cover, and 3D vegetation structure, exhibited nonlinear or conditional associations with avian metrics. In particular, associations involving roof 3D vegetation structure varied with roof floor, roof grass coverage, and surrounding vegetation cover. Our findings advance large-scale understanding of roof-bird associations and underscore the importance of jointly considering both horizontal and vertical structural elements within a multiscale framework. The study provides evidence-based insights for designing biodiversity-friendly green roofs that consider broader urban vegetatio…

papers.title: Model–Observation Discrepancies in the Coupling of Vegetation Greening and Transpiration Under Rising Vapor Pressure Deficit
papers.abstract: Abstract Vapor pressure deficit (VPD), a key indicator of atmospheric dryness, has markedly increased across most global land areas due to progressive warming. Although site‐scale studies show that increasing VPD may enhance plant transpiration (Tran) and influence water and energy fluxes between land and atmosphere, this relationship has not been thoroughly investigated on the global scale. Here, we apply a binning approach to quantify the contribution of VPD to global Tran by ruling out the effect of soil moisture. To this aim, we integrate satellite‐based observations, reanalysis data sets, and simulations from sixteen Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models into a coherent framework. VPD shows a broadly positive influence on Tran over most parts of the global land consistently across all data sets. Exceptions occur in tropical rainforests where reanalysis data and CMIP6 model outputs suggest a negative VPD‐Tran interplay. Attribution analysis suggests that increasing leaf area index reduces the positive effect of VPD on Tran in reanalysis data sets and CMIP6 models compared to satellite‐based observations. This discrepancy may reflect differences in the representation of the effective canopy‐level response to high atmospheric water demand, potentially involving stomatal regulation, plant hydraulics, and vegetation structure. Such differences may contribute to an underestimated transpiration response to VPD. These findings highlight the need to better represent physiological processes, hydraulic processes, and vegetation structural characteristics in process‐based models to capture vegetation responses to increasing water stress.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Simultaneous ToF/FMCW LiDAR Using a Dual‐Mode Light Source in a Single Architecture
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Light detection and ranging (LiDAR) systems are increasingly required to provide long‐range operation, high axial resolution, and velocity estimation within a single platform. However, conventional time‐of‐flight (ToF) and frequency‐modulated continuous‐wave (FMCW) methods demand a high electrical bandwidth to satisfy these requirements simultaneously. Here, we present a simultaneous ToF/FMCW LiDAR enabled by a dual‐mode light source that alternately generates nanosecond pulses and FMCW waveforms through synchronized optical‐intensity and frequency‐modulation. This single‐architecture design enables concurrent acquisition of time‐domain ToF and spectral‐domain FMCW ranging without additional optical paths or auxiliary light sources. Under bandwidth‐limited conditions, ToF measurement maintained absolute distance accuracy despite a loss of resolution, whereas the FMCW measurement preserved high axial resolution but experienced aliasing due to subsampling. By integrating these complementary datasets through a reconstruction algorithm, the system achieves high‐resolution short‐range performance together with alias‐free long‐range detection. Moreover, Doppler analysis of the FMCW interferograms verified accurate velocity estimation within the Nyquist limit. These results demonstrate that a dual‐mode light source can unify ToF and FMCW ranging in a compact single architecture, overcoming electrical bandwidth constraints while enabling simultaneous distance and velocity measurements.

papers.title: Toward Consistent Canopy Characterization From Low‐Cost UAV Imagery
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring tropical forest structure at landscape scale requires cost‐effective methods capable of bridging the gap between field inventories and satellite remote sensing products. However, the diversity of available individual tree crown (ITC) segmentation algorithms raises questions about the consistency and reliability of derived structural metrics—a critical issue for any ecological application relying on these outputs. We evaluated three ITC segmentation algorithms—Detectree2, SAM, and the hybrid Detectree2SAM (D2S)—applied to very high‐resolution RGB orthomosaics (5 cm resolution) acquired over ~200 ha of the Luki Biosphere Reserve (Democratic Republic of Congo) using a low‐cost drone. Algorithms were validated at the individual scale against a photointerpretation reference of 1882 manually delineated crowns and at the plot scale against a field inventory of 360 trees across 18 plots. At the individual scale, IoU‐based F1 scores ranged from 0.57 (D2S) to 0.67 (SAM), revealing clear precision–recall trade‐offs. At the plot scale, D2S provided the most accurate crown area estimates (RMSD = 26%–29%), while SAM best reproduced canopy density (RMSD = 22%). All three algorithms systematically overestimated aggregated metrics; a linear correction substantially reduced prediction errors and improved cross‐algorithm convergence, yielding consistent estimates—median crown area of the 20 largest trees (~148 m 2 ), total crown area (~3850 m 2 per plot), and canopy density (~80 ind/ha). Agreement maps revealed systematic spatial divergences, including edge artifacts, SAM's tendency to underestimate canopy density, and localized overestimation of crown areas in disturbed stands. Raw ITC outputs carry substantial systematic biases requiring explicit field‐calibrated correction before ecological use. We propose a three‐step operational pipeline—(i) plot‐scale field validation, (ii) per‐algorithm linear bias correction, and (iii) landscape‐scale aggregation—that reduces inter‐algorithm divergence and delivers consistent, ecologically interpretable structural estimates from low‐cost UAV imagery.

papers.title: Cross-species evaluation: Reindeer as an ecological evaluator of a satellite-based lichen cover map
papers.abstract: Accurate maps of resources are important tools in wildlife and animal range management yet validating them across large spatial extents remains a challenge. We leveraged fine-scale GPS tracking of consumers and a strong consumer-resource relationship to perform large-scale evaluation of a resource map. Our aim was to present the first high-resolution ground lichen cover map for the Sámi reindeer winter grazing area in Sweden, and to complement traditional model validation methods by using 680,000 reindeer GPS relocations and the consumer-resource relationship between reindeer ( Rangifer tarandus tarandus ) and ground lichens for ecological evaluation. We expected a successful map to be reflected in the reindeer use of lichen, and that predicted lichen cover would be a significant predictor in habitat selection models. The map was produced using a Generalised Additive Model trained on National Forest Inventory field data with Sentinel-2 imagery, forest variables, and soil type as predictors. The model explained 57.4% of the total variance in lichen cover. Our analyses supported both expectations: hurdle models showed that the odds of predicted lichen presence were 44% higher at reindeer-used than available locations, and used locations had 15% more predicted lichen cover than available locations. Integrated step-selection analyses confirmed consistent selection for predicted lichen cover, and adding the lichen map outperformed a simpler model including topographic and movement variables. Best performance was achieved combining predicted lichen cover with land cover classification. Our cross-species evaluation approach offers a complement to traditional statistical validation, applicable to other systems with strong consumer-resource relationships.

papers.title: Composite Degradation Index Reveals Type-Specific Drivers of Forest Decline on Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
papers.abstract: Forest degradation assessments are constrained by single-dimensional indicators (e.g., NDVI) that fail to simultaneously capture functional degradation (biomass loss) and structural degradation (landscape fragmentation), while type-specific management responses remain poorly operationalized. To address this gap, we developed a Composite Degradation Index (CDI) integrating biomass dynamics (Biomass Slope) and a forest fragmentation index (FFI). The CDI was applied at a 30 m spatial resolution using MODIS NDVI/EVI, SRTM DEM, and land-use data from 2000 to 2020 across coniferous, broad-leaved, and mixed forests across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) to quantify degradation severity, identify nonlinear response thresholds, and project fragmentation trends under CMIP6 scenarios using natural breaks classification. Random Forest, XGBoost, and SHAP analysis disentangled the relative contributions of climatic factors, topography, and human activities. The CDI improved assessment accuracy by 22% relative to NDVI. Coniferous forests exhibited strong sensitivity to warming (5.2% per +1 °C), with 27% of degradation indirectly linked to permafrost thaw. Broad-leaved forests responded most strongly to precipitation variability (3.8% per +10%), reflecting hydraulic stress and habitat connectivity loss. Mixed forests showed the highest anthropogenic degradation (35% contribution), highlighting ecotonal fragmentation. Under SSP5-8.5, severe fragmentation is projected to reach 21.73% by 2060; moderate mitigation delays extreme fragmentation by 1.6 years. The CDI provides a transferable framework for “threshold diagnosis–attribution–zoning intervention” in the QTP and analogous vulnerable ecosystems. Based on type-specific response thresholds, we propose three management strategies: (i) permafrost monitoring and thermal buffering for coniferous forests; (ii) hydrological connectivity conservation for broad-leaved forests; and (iii) anthropogenic disturbance buffers for mixed forests. This study demonstrates that composite indicators can bridge environmental monitoring and sustainability decision-making, directly contributing to SDG 13 and SDG 15.

papers.title: Dynamicity of Stand‐Scale Transpiration and Its Controlling Factors: Insights From Mixed‐Conifer Mediterranean Headwater Catchments
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The mixed‐conifer forests of Sierra Nevada create a complex system of water, energy and nutrient cycling. Thus, this study aims to understand the spatial and temporal variability of soil moisture and stand‐scale transpiration across three central Sierra headwater catchments and their controlling factors. The mean daily average sap flow of Abies concolor varies from 0.69 ± 0.48 to 1.27 ± 0.72 L/h. Higher spatial variability in soil moisture and stand‐scale transpiration was found in the snowmelt period, followed by the soil moisture recession period when vegetation growth is not water limited. The daily average sap flow was higher on south aspect than on north aspect, but this pattern was not consistent across all seasons. The diel pattern of the sap flow revealed a larger contribution of nocturnal sap flow during the dry period (22.3%–37.8%) and a smaller contribution during the recession period (16.3%–23.9%) across all catchments. Multiple linear regression analysis suggests that sap flow during summer (recession period) was governed by the ecosystem's energy, indicated in part by vapour pressure deficit and temperature. Soil moisture regulated the subsequent dry‐period transpiration. The energy‐limited condition in winter restricted the transpiration even when sufficient soil moisture was available. Topography, explained by topographic positioning index ( tpi ), played a major role in explaining stand‐scale transpiration, especially during higher atmospheric demand periods, whereas tree size (i.e., DBH) explained more than 10% sap flow variance in all seasons. The findings of this study will provide the basis for a better understanding of the eco‐hydrological processes of the Sierra Nevada under natural and anthropogenic‐induced changes.
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

papers.title: Assessing the resilience of coastal vegetation ecosystem through carbon storage dynamics using Landsat time series
papers.abstract: Due to increasing habitat fragmentation and persistent land-cover dynamics, assessing resilience in coastal vegetation ecosystems poses substantial challenges. To address these issues, this study quantifies the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of vegetation carbon storage to evaluate ecosystem resilience in complex coastal habitats. By integrating long-term Landsat time-series data on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform with the Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model, we developed an integrated framework for assessing coastal vegetation resilience. Taking the coastal zone of Jiangsu Province as the study area, the results indicate the following: (1) By integrating critical factors such as phenological variability, tidal inundation, and land–water interactions, the proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of vegetation information extraction and the reliability of long-term carbon storage monitoring in complex coastal environments; (2) From 1985 to 2024, the total vegetation carbon storage in Jiangsu Province exhibited a fluctuating upward trend, rising from 1258.08 Tg to 1514.41 Tg, marking a net gain of 256.33 Tg (20.38 %). This suggests that coastal vegetation maintains robust long-term carbon sequestration capacity amid cultivated land dominance and enhanced forest carbon sinks; (3) Spatially, the evolution of vegetation carbon storage revealed a distinct pattern of “North–South differentiation and Land–Sea coupling.” Specifically, the northern plains and coastal zones showed continuous growth and steadily strengthened carbon sink functions, whereas the highly urbanized southern region experienced greater constraints and more pronounced fluctuations. Resilience assessments indicated stronger recovery elasticity and maintenance capacity in the north, relatively weaker resilience and higher sensitivity to disturbances in the south, and a transitional coastal type characterized by high recovery potential but weak stability; (4) The provincial-scale increase in vegetation carbon storage was primarily driven by the structural upgrading of vegetation coverage classes. Specifically, the significant expansi…

papers.title: Autonomous UAVs in Critical Infrastructure Inspection: Empirical Evaluation, Reporting Standard, and Implications for Strategic Decisions
papers.abstract: Purpose: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become a mature tool for remote sensing data acquisition for critical infrastructure (IC) inspections, particularly in the energy, transportation, bridge infrastructure, water networks and industrial installation sectors.The aim of the article is to synthetically capture the results of empirical research: field inspection missions using RGB, thermal imaging (TIR) and LiDAR sensors, as well as automatic data analytics (deep learning) to detect defects and anomalies.Design/Methodology/Approach: In the methodological part, a unified scheme for reporting empirical research (mission parameters, method of obtaining the "reference truth", quality metrics and operational utility indicators) is proposed, as well as a framework for integrating results with crisis management processes (time-to-assessment, false dispositions, repair priorities).

papers.title: Annual canopy height mapping in Italy from Landsat and multi-source LiDAR for disturbance and recovery monitoring
papers.abstract: Accurate and continuous monitoring of forest canopy height is essential for assessing forest structure, biomass, disturbance, and recovery. However, airborne laser scanning (ALS) has incomplete national coverage, is updated infrequently, and is costly to acquire. Here, we present an annual 30 m canopy height dataset for Italy spanning 2004–2024, developed by integrating Landsat imagery with multi-source LiDAR observations in a time-series deep learning framework. Two U-Net models were trained independently using canopy height reference data from ALS and NASA's Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) spaceborne LiDAR mission. Annual canopy height predictions from the two models were then fused using Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) to improve spatial consistency and temporal continuity. Validation against field measurements from the Italian National Forest Inventory (NFI) showed high predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 3.98 m. Despite its coarser spatial resolution, our 30 m product outperformed canopy height products currently available in Italy, including a Europe-scale PlanetScope-based dataset at 3 m resolution and a global Sentinel-based canopy height product at 10 m resolution, while also providing a harmonized annual record over two decades rather than only one or a few years. In contrast, an existing Europe-scale Landsat-based product yielded a low R 2 in this mountainous region, highlighting the limited transferability of broad-scale models in complex terrain. To demonstrate the utility of the dataset for forest dynamics monitoring, we derived a canopy height change-based disturbance product and evaluated it against independent observed events, obtaining a mean precision of 0.64 for 2005–2016. We also quantified post-disturbance recovery by tracking canopy height regrowth in areas disturbed during 2004–2005 across major Italian biomes through 2024. These results show that combining Landsat time series, multi-source LiDAR, deep learning, and Bayesian fusion provides an effective framework for annual canopy height mapping and for monitoring forest disturbance and recovery. The final dataset is publicly available via Zenodo and offers a…

papers.title: Intercomparison of Global Solar Induced Chlorophyl Fluorescence Products
papers.abstract: Abstract Satellite observations of Sun‐Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence (SIF) provide a powerful means to assess terrestrial photosynthesis at regional to global scales, yet major SIF products differ in retrieval strategy, radiometric stability, and sensitivity to environmental conditions. We evaluate four widely used SIF data sets—Continuous Solar‐Induced Fluorescence (CSIF), Global OCO‐2 SIF (GOSIF), SIF005, and OCO‐005—across multiple biomes, climate regimes, and temporal scales by comparing them against tower‐derived gross primary production (GPP), tower‐observed SIF, and independent climate anomalies. Across FLUXNET sites, all SIF data sets show robust linear relationships with annual GPP ( R 2 = 0.64–0.71), with strongest performance in forested ecosystems and increased scatter in water‐limited landscapes. Monthly analyses in northern high latitudes reveal exceptionally strong SIF–GPP coupling ( R 2 up to 0.87), demonstrating SIF's ability to capture rapid seasonal transitions in boreal and tundra productivity. Drought evaluations in the Sahel and Amazon show that GOSIF and Continuous Solar‐Induced Fluorescence (CSIF) most accurately track rainfall‐driven reductions in photosynthesis, while SIF005 displays weaker and noisier responses. Long‐term trend analyses north of 50°N reveal consistent early‐ and late‐season productivity increases in GOSIF, CSIF, and FLUXCOM‐X GPP, whereas SIF005 diverges substantially, underscoring limitations for climate‐trend detection in high‐latitude environments. Comparisons with tower‐measured SIF further confirm the physical fidelity of the satellite data sets, with GOSIF and OCO‐005 showing the strongest agreement. Overall, SIF is a reliable proxy for ecosystem productivity across diverse environmental settings, but performance varies among products. CSIF and GOSIF generally showed the most consistent behavior across seasons, climatic extremes, and regions, whereas SIF005 exhibited greater noise and less consistent trend behavior.
